title: Regional quantized-model context mismatch causing tokens/sec collapse — emergency QoS and graceful model downshift
creator: Diego Morales
description:
Summary: Several enterprise customers (mix of Hosted, Dedicated, Private) reported a sharp drop in tokens/sec and TTFT regressions when using our new int8 quantized variants on long-context workloads (>4k tokens). Impact: affected requests show 30-80% tokens/sec collapse and elevated TTFT on long continuations; customers experienced timeouts and raised priority escalations. Scope: multi-region but concentrated in eu-west and us-east regions; models affected are the new quant-int8 variants of rdx-large and rdx-bert-extended running on mixed GPU pools where kernel selection falls back to a legacy fused-attn path.

Root cause hypothesis: During transition to int8 kernels we introduced a context-stride mapping change in the KV serialization layer. For long-context requests the kv-cache segments are misaligned when the runtime selects the legacy fused-attn kernel (fallback path) rather than the new quantized kernel. This causes repeated cache misses and a regeneration loop that effectively throttles token emission. The issue is amplified on Dedicated and Private clusters that have heterogeneous driver/kernel versions and a percentage of hosts that still report the legacy kernel capability.

Short-term mitigation plan (this ticket): 1) Emergency QoS shaping: throttle long-context queues for affected variants to protect other tenants and reduce cascading token starvation. 2) Graceful downshift: implement a fast-path that detects the kv alignment mismatch and dynamically downshifts affected requests to the non-quantized (fp16) runtime for that request only. 3) Region-level pinning: temporarily pin the quantized variants off hosts reporting legacy kernel capability in eu-west and us-east. 4) Monitoring/alerts: create dedicated Grafana panels and SLO alerts for tokens/sec differential and TTFT for variants. 5) Customer bridge: coordinate with SRE/CS to inform impacted customers and provide ETA.

Notes: this ticket is an emergency engineering response to customer escalations; follow-up epic will track the root-cause permanent fix in the kernel selection and KV serialization codepaths.
reproduction_steps: 1) Use a long-context prompt > 4k tokens with rdx-large-int8 in eu-west region
2) Observe initial token bursts then sustained tokens/sec drop to 20-40% of baseline after token 512
3) Correlate with host capability tag 'legacy-fused-attn' in trace metadata
4) Re-run same workload on pinned fp16 hosts to confirm tokens/sec stabilizes
acceptance_criteria: Emergency QoS shaping deployed to eu-west and us-east within 6 hours and reduces noisy neighbor impact
Per-request graceful downshift implemented and tested (unit + integration) so affected requests finish with fp16 fallback without error
Region pinning applied and validated (no new failures reported by customers for pinned hosts)
Dashboards updated and alert thresholds configured for TTFT and tokens/sec deltas
Customer-facing incident notes and ETA posted to incident channel and CS ticket threads
